title: What The Banjo Knows — EN/FR/PT (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 105bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal French Portuguese Appalachian African philosophy language learning
lyrics:
[Verse 1 — English]
The banjo arrived in America from West Africa originally
Which surprises people who assume it's exclusively hillbilly
The five-string banjo in the mountains of Appalachia
Developed its own dialect and chose to stay right there

[Verse 2 — French, with English translation]
Le banjo est né en Afrique avant d'aller en Amérique
[The banjo was born in Africa before going to America]
Il a traversé les mers avec la mémoire afrique
[It crossed the seas carrying African memory]
Les Appalaches l'ont adopté comme leur instrument propre
[The Appalachians adopted it as their own instrument]
Le banjo sait qu'il appartient à un peuple noble
[The banjo knows it belongs to a noble people]

[Chorus — English]
What does the banjo know that I don't know?
It knows the shortest distance between Africa and Carolina's flow
What does the banjo know on the mountain side?
It knows that music travels further than the people who supplied
That's my boy

[Bridge — Portuguese, with English translation]
O banjo veio da África para as montanhas americanas
[The banjo came from Africa to the American mountains]
Cruzou oceanos, desfiladeiros e savanas
[It crossed oceans, gorges and savannas]
Hoje toca nos Apalaches com sotaque de lá
[Today it plays in the Appalachians with an accent from there]
O banjo sabe de onde veio e para onde vai voltar
[The banjo knows where it came from and where it will return]

[Outro — All three languages]
What the banjo knows… Ce que le banjo sait… O que o banjo sabe
Africa to Appalachia — Afrique vers Appalaches — África para os Apalaches
That's my boy
